paper_summary: Aluminium 2024 matrix syntactic foams were made by vacuum casting (-1 bar vacuum, 560 C, then 15 bar argon pressure, three-step mould filling with vibration) around packed beds of three low-cost lightweight porous aggregates sieved to 2.5-4.5 mm: expanded perlite, LECA (expanded clay) and pumice. Foam densities were 1.09, 1.385 and 2.05 g/cm3 with aggregate volume fractions of 66.8, 62.8 and 50.0% and total porosities of 62.6, 50.5 and 33.2%. Quasi-static uniaxial compression (ISO 13314) gave plateau stresses of 14.12, 19.31 and 31.1 MPa, unloading moduli of 3.97, 6.19 and 7.2 GPa, densification strains of 65, 69 and 60%, energy absorption of 5.4, 11.2 and 17.5 MJ/m3 and energy absorption efficiencies of 66, 70.5 and 79% at 50% strain; compressive properties and energy absorption rose with density, and low-density foams failed in a shear band while high-density pumice foam deformed uniformly.

structure.microstructure_notes: Total porosity of the foam F_TP = 62.55% (Table 3); the expanded perlite particles themselves are about 92% porous with a solid-phase density of 2.81 g/cm3. Aggregates are evenly distributed with a distinct boundary to the matrix; aluminium did not penetrate the aggregate cavities and no debonding was seen. Table 3 lists the foam density as 1.09 g/cm3. This lower-density foam deformed locally along a large shear band.

extraction_notes: PRIMARY DATA (3 records): from Table 3 (physical) and Table 4 (mechanical). modulus_mpa is the unloading elastic modulus E_UL (GPa x 1000); the quasi-elastic gradient QE is given in test.specimen_notes because the schema has only one modulus field. plateau_stress_mpa is sigma_Pl (ISO 13314 mean stress over 20-40% strain); sigma_Ple (= 1.3 x sigma_Pl, 18.36 / 25.10 / 40.43 MPa) is a derived quantity and was not stored, and no sigma_max was reported for the authors' own samples, so strength_mpa is null for the primary records. densification_strain is epsilon_Ple converted from % to fraction (0.65 / 0.69 / 0.60). INCONSISTENCIES IN THE PAPER: (a) the abstract states energy absorption efficiencies of 85 / 78 / 70% for perlite / LECA / pumice, which contradicts Table 4 and the conclusion (66 / 70.5 / 79%); the Table 4 values were used. (b) the abstract calls 0.24, 0.55 and 1.30 g/cm3 the foam densities, but Table 3 shows these are the aggregate densities and the foam densities are 1.09, 1.35 and 2.05 g/cm3. (c) the LECA foam density is 1.35 in Table 3 and 1.385 in Table 4; Table 4 was used for measured_density_g_cc and Table 3 is noted in microstructure_notes. (d) particle size is given as 2.5-4.5 mm in Sec. 3.1 but 4.75-6.30 mm on p. 7; because of that conflict and because no mean was stated, particle_mean_diameter_um was left null. particle_true_density_g_cc holds the aggregate (particle) density from Table 3; the skeletal/solid-phase densities (2.81, 2.95, 3.6 g/cm3) and the particle porosities (92, 80, 64%) are in microstructure_notes. The total foam porosity F_TP was NOT put in matrix_porosity_fraction because that field means unintended matrix voids, whereas F_TP here is the intended aggregate porosity; it is recorded in microstructure_notes. Test temperature and strain rate were not stated (only 'quasi-static'), so both are null. SECONDARY DATA (16 records): 14 rows of Table 1 (a literature comparison table) plus two values quoted in the introduction (Bonabi et al. ref. 29 and Taherishargh et al. ref. 31); all are marked data_origin=secondary with the cited reference in sample_label. Table 1 was not machine-parsed into a [TABLE] block in the text file, so its evidence quotes are the row values reassembled in column order from the linearised text. Manufacturing routes without a matching enum value (gravity infiltration casting, pressureless infiltration, melt infiltration, DMD, counter-gravity casting) were mapped to process_route='other' and named in specimen_notes / microstructure_notes. CAVEAT ON PARTICLE TYPE: perlite, LECA and pumice are porous (non-hollow, irregular) lightweight aggregates rather than true hollow microspheres, so particle_type='other' was used for them; the paper nevertheless classifies the resulting materials as metal matrix syntactic foams.
